plan: [ This is effectively a second‑price (Vickrey) auction: final price equals the second‑highest sealed bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Underbidding risks losing profitably when the clock is below my value; overbidding risks winning at a price above my value if a rival’s bid lies between my value and my inflated bid. Tie-breaking is random; bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit. Therefore, I will set my exit price equal to my value. ]

[ This is effectively a second‑price auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second‑highest bid. With independent private values and one round, the dominant strategy to maximize expected profit is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks winning and paying above value; underbidding risks losing when profitable. Therefore, set my sealed bid equal to 15 so I win exactly when my value is highest and pay the next‑highest bid, ensuring non‑negative profit if I win and zero otherwise. ]

This is a second-price auction via an ascending clock: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Truthful bidding wins whenever my value is highest and pays at most the second-highest value. Overbidding risks negative profit; underbidding sacrifices positive surplus. I will bid 10.
